title: Show Season
tagline: Signs, badges, shirts and booth kits, ready before the doors open.
what: I run the marketing for a convention the company hosts every spring, and get us ready for the trade shows around it, at home and overseas.
does: Plan the hosted convention from ticket launch to post-event survey
Keep the events calendar, event pages and countdowns current
Brief the designer on every sign, shirt, lanyard and badge
Order and track the print and swag: badges, lanyards, shirts, bags
Build sponsor pages, signs and a looping highlight slideshow
Make backdrops, table throws, banners and posters for each trade show
Translate and print brochures and signs for shows overseas
Pack and label show shipments, and run giveaways at the booth

solved.problem: Overseas shows need brochures and signs in other languages and in local paper sizes, and ordering them from home does not work.
solved.did: I had materials translated and resized for local formats, and found printers near each show.
solved.ended: The signs and brochures were at the show on time, in the right language.

solved.problem: Signs and booth equipment needed to reach the same pack list.
solved.did: I merged the lists so everything for a booth flows into one load-out and print list.
solved.ended: Everything for a booth now ships from one list.

solved.problem: A sponsor slideshow is only as reliable as the venue Wi-Fi.
solved.did: I built an animated sponsor site instead of a flat slide deck, and made it run offline.
solved.ended: It played in the main hall, after I demoed it to leadership.

solved.problem: A giant backdrop looked soft and would not hold up at 20 feet.
solved.did: I rebuilt it from a higher resolution original, then ordered it in time to ship ahead to the show.
solved.ended: It arrived ahead of the show.

tools.name: Event editor
tools.line: the event team adds or changes an event and every page showing it updates.

tools.name: Show packing page
tools.line: numbered totes, a pick list and shipping labels for a show shipment, used by the warehouse.

tools.name: Sponsor slideshow site
tools.line: an animated showcase that still runs if the Wi-Fi drops.

tools.name: Event page for the team
tools.line: equipment, signs and shipping for each event in one view.

worksWith: Leadership, the event team, a contract designer, the warehouse, accounting, print vendors, a translator, venue staff.
story: The convention drew over 600 registrations and 94% checked in. For the outside shows, the warehouse used my packing page on a real shipment: numbered totes, a pick list and a label for each box.
The schedule, signs, shirts and lanyards had lived on separate lists, with someone retyping changes onto the website.

I built an event editor the team could use themselves, then a page with equipment, signs and shipping side by side. Lanyards, swag bags, sponsor signs and flyers went out together, with a tracking sheet for the people on site.
The event team keeps the pages current and the warehouse can pack a show without asking me to assemble another list.
credit: The job, plus the tools I built for it
